name: Lizzo
notes: Brass-and-piano funk-pop with rapped verses. The entry is explicit about the one thing that could have gone wrong here: the hat rolls are trap-derived but the backbeat is *not* half-time — "trap-derived hat rolls over a straight backbeat rather than half-time" — so `halfTime` is false at `backbeat_24` while `rolls.vocab` keeps 16ths and 32nds at a high `freqPerBar`. The rest of the drum block is the entry's: "trap-lite kick and clap with 16th/32nd hat rolls under a glittering piano loop as the lead element; handclaps and finger snaps on the backbeat; live-feel tom fills as section markers", which is the `snap` stack, the `tom` perc lanes and the roll ladder switched off because the fills are toms. The 808 is authored because the entry names it — "808 sub with short slides sitting under a piano loop; the low end is simple so the piano and brass read" — as `counter_riff` with a low slide probability and a bassline held simple at a high `followRootsProb`. Harmony is "2-bar piano-loop vamps" over "major-mode with blues-third melodic borrowing", so `harmonicRhythm` is vamp-led and `major_blues` carries real weight with `colorTones` on the flat third. The melody block encodes the documented duality: "toplines alternate rapped, speech-rhythm verses with sung, gospel-inflected belted choruses", which is the widest `densityPerBar` in this batch (4—14) and a wide register; "backing vocals are gang-chant style" plus "flute as a signature solo timbre and horn stabs" is the `answer_lick` counter. ⚠ `confidence` is medium against a medium-high rating because "tempo/key bands inferred": every drum probability, the humanize numbers and `bpm.mode` 110 (the midpoint of the stated 95—125 band) are INFERRED, and the entry's [LOW-CONF] mark on the belt/rap register claim is repeated here. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 943/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** The 1-bar value came out of `melody.phraseBars`, which is now [2,4] weighted [3,2]. `generators::melody` writes a phrase's rhythm **once** and reuses it for every repeat, so a 1-bar phrase gives the whole clip one bar of rhythmic entropy — and the counter, whose onsets are read off the lead's, inherits that ceiling. Distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "2-bar piano-loop vamps, plus flute as a signature solo timbre and horn stabs; toplines alternate rapped, speech-rhythm verses with sung, gospel-inflected belted choruses. Backing vocals are gang-chant style.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
